note: Every view and projection the Markets Desk has made, newest first, with the news that bears on each, until it is right, wrong or closed. Never delete an entry: a wrong call stays on the record, marked wrong.

views.title: Juhayna returns to EGP 27–28 by end of January
views.detail: Nine-month profit rose 60% to EGP 2.04bn on sales up 25% to EGP 27.66bn (Mubasher), showing price rises held volumes; at EGP 24.95 the stock sits at its 50-day average of about EGP 24.84, below its 52-week high of about EGP 27.63. Consumer demand cracking under price rises is the risk.

views.title: Chip stocks stay under pressure into Apple's results
views.detail: Intel fell 28.6%, Qualcomm 11.1%, Broadcom 5.5% and Nvidia 4.2% on Friday as investors question AI spending; Nvidia is at its lowest since 1 August.

updates.text: Intel guided fourth-quarter revenue to $15bn–$16bn against about $17bn expected; Qualcomm fell 11% and Broadcom 5.5%.
The semiconductor index fell about 3.4% on Monday and Nvidia closed at $202.06, its lowest since 1 August; Apple fell about 3% after hours.
Nvidia rose 2.3% and Broadcom 3.1% on Tuesday; AMD rose 5–7% after hours on better-than-expected earnings.
Nvidia fell 3.2% to $200.13 on Wednesday, its lowest close since 31 July, while Asian chip stocks sold off.
Nasdaq fell 5.5% into a correction and chips lost about 12% on Thursday; Nvidia closed at $182.29.

Nvidia rose 2.8% to $186.64 as chips bounced after Thursday's rout, still 8.8% below the $204.64 start; Microsoft's retreat from rented AI capacity and Microchip's 10% fall on guidance keep the pressure on the sector.
The FT reported US officials believe Jensen Huang was close to an alleged Chinese spy; House chairs want a briefing on November 18, a political risk to Nvidia's China sales.
Nvidia's board opened an independent inquiry into Jensen Huang, a week before results; the shares slipped about 2.4% overnight.
Nvidia fell 4.3% to $178.67, its lowest since April, on its board's inquiry into Jensen Huang, while other chip stocks rose 6.9%; the call tracks Nvidia, so it stands.
Nvidia fell 5.5% to $168.89, its lowest close since March, as the board's inquiry into Jensen Huang continued; Broadcom rose 3.9%.

views.title: Developers lag while rates stay high
views.detail: Dearer financing hits instalment buyers and developers' own borrowing; Talaat Moustafa and Palm Hills should trail the EGX30.
views.wrong: Talaat Moustafa and Palm Hills beat the EGX30 over four weeks.

updates.text: Talaat Moustafa signed an EGP 11 trillion development deal with the state for four projects.
Al Ahly Pharos put Palm Hills' fair value at EGP 21.40, well above its price.
Talaat Moustafa closed at EGP 79.50 and Palm Hills at EGP 10.60 (−7.0%, lowest since April).
Talaat Moustafa fell 1.9% to EGP 78.00 and Palm Hills was flat at EGP 10.60; both are below their starting levels while the EGX30 is down 2.4%.
Palm Hills rose 6.8% to EGP 11.32 and Talaat Moustafa 2.3% to EGP 79.80 on Tuesday, in line with the EGX30's month so far; contractual property sales reached EGP 1.048 trillion in nine months.
Palm Hills fell 0.4% and Orascom Development 0.5% while the EGX30 rose 2.8%.
Palm Hills rose 5.7% and Talaat Moustafa 2.7% on Thursday, beating the EGX30's 1.0%; Emaar Misr awarded an EGP 7.1bn Marassi Red contract.
On the week Talaat Moustafa rose 3.54% and Palm Hills 4.47%, ahead of the EGX30's 3.1% (Youm7); fixed certificates at 18.75% from Sunday add competition for savings.
An insider sold 443,600 Palm Hills shares on Sunday; both developers remain below their 50-day averages.

views.title: Money rotates from AI spenders to steady earners
views.detail: After Alphabet's fall, investors favour predictable earnings (Walmart, JPMorgan) over heavy AI spenders.
views.wrong: Alphabet and Amazon beat Walmart and JPMorgan over four weeks.

updates.text: Amazon and Intel fell after the bell on earnings misses, deepening the AI-spending sell-off.
Money left technology on Friday while Walmart rose 1.9% to $123.51 and Alphabet fell 1.4% to $279.84.
Walmart rose 3.4% to $127.69 (+5.3% since 30 Oct), Visa and Costco rose, Oracle fell 8.8% and chipmakers 3.4%: money moved from AI names to steady earners.
Microsoft, Nvidia and Oracle rebounded on Tuesday while Walmart fell 2.2%; the 10-year yield rose to 4.96%.
Walmart rose 3.5% to $129.17 and Alphabet 3.2% to $288.93 as megacaps rallied on the midterm result.
Nasdaq fell 5.5% into a correction and chips lost about 12% on Thursday; Nvidia closed at $182.29.
Walmart fell 1.7% to $125.52 as money rotated back into rebounding tech, with no company news (Investing.com); Alphabet rose 0.8%. A reminder that the rotation reverses on tech bounces.
Costco's October sales rose 12.6% and comparable sales 11.1%, while Microsoft is ending a 2023 AI capacity deal with Oracle: steady earners keep delivering as AI spenders retrench.
Costco declared a $30 special dividend and a $4bn buyback (company filing) and Berkshire's B shares closed at a record, while Alphabet slipped 0.3% to $287.38 after a hot CPI.

views.title: Higher rates protect CIB's margins
views.detail: High rates protect lending margins and T-bill income; CIB should hold up better than the market.
views.wrong: CIB falls more than the EGX30 over the next two weeks.

updates.text: The central bank raised its key rates by 100 basis points, to 20.00% for deposits and 21.00% for lending.
CIB fell 2.1% to EGP 118.00, its lowest since March, as the EGX30 lost 1.7%.
On Monday the central bank sold the dollar at EGP 55.51 (from 56.04 on 30 Oct) and CIB rose 2.9% to EGP 121.40, above its EGP 120.47 start, though the EGX30 fell to 48,403.
CIB rose 2.5% to EGP 126.51, outpacing its 2.1% gain since 30 October on the EGX30.
Central bank dollar rate fell for a sixth session to EGP 54.01; CIB rose to EGP 128.00.
CIB rose 6.25% on the week to EGP 128.00 on EGP 2.47bn of trading (Youm7), and October inflation eased to 12.0% against a 20% deposit rate, widening the real yield banks earn.
CIB's deputy chief executive said its Yomo digital bank has preliminary central bank approval; results are expected Wednesday.

CIB's nine-month profit rose 1.6% to EGP 63.1bn, 18% on an underlying basis, but its quarterly margin narrowed to 8.02% from 8.40% for the nine months, before the October 29 hike could help; the results are in line rather than a test of the call.
CIB rose 2.3% to EGP 131.00, 8.7% above the view's start against the EGX30's 5.8%; management said it expects rate cuts to be delayed, which keeps margins wide.

views.title: Gas rationing keeps fertilizer stocks under pressure through November
views.detail: Gas to fertiliser plants was cut 20% from 1 November; urea prices ($535 a ton) cover part of the volume loss, but Abu Qir and Mopco have run hard this year and fell four sessions in a row.
views.wrong: Abu Qir closes above EGP 85, or the gas allocations are restored in full.

updates.text: Kima reported a 20% cut from 1 November; Abu Qir said it reduced intake; Mopco is adjusting to available gas.
Abu Qir rose 3.0% to EGP 80.00 and Mopco 3.2% to EGP 41.37 after four falls; the gas cut remains in force.
Abu Qir confirmed a gas-supply cut from November 1 and reorganized production; Mopco and KIMA report 20% cuts.

The government raised gas cuts for fertilizer and methanol plants to 33% from 20%, with no end date, to save on LNG cargoes near $120m each; Abu Qir fell 5.8% to EGP 76.30. A deeper, open-ended cut makes the call more likely.

views.title: The EGX30 holds above 49,255 while foreign institutions keep buying
views.detail: The EGX30 rose 2.83% to 50,650.18 with foreign institutions net buyers; it needs follow-through on higher turnover and a good T-bill auction.

updates.text: Wall Street steadied on Friday (Nasdaq +1.09%) after Thursday's 4.4% S&P 500 fall, easing the risk-off threat to Sunday's reopening; the EGX30 ended the week at 51,152.73, up 3.1%.
The EGX30 fell 0.67% to 50,812.07 on Sunday as foreign investors sold a net EGP 27.9m, a small amount against EGP 10.5bn traded.
The EGX30 rose 1.19% to 51,414.93 on Monday, but foreigners sold a net EGP 302.8m while Egyptians bought EGP 347.8m, so the foreign buying the call rested on has turned to selling.
Foreigners turned net buyers of EGP 42.1m as the EGX30 rose 2.08% to 52,483.46 on EGP 12.8bn of turnover (Masrawy, Al Mal).

views.title: The pound stays firmer than EGP 56 per dollar into the IMF review
views.detail: A cheaper barrel and a wide real yield (one-year bill 26.08% against 13.9% inflation) keep foreign holders in Egyptian debt.
views.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 56 (central bank sell rate).

updates.text: Central bank dollar rate fell for a sixth session to EGP 54.01; CIB rose to EGP 128.00.
Inflation eased to 12.0% in October from 12.8%, widening the real yield on the 26.03% one-year bill to about 14 points.
A strong US jobs report lifted the dollar index 0.7% to 102.28, near its 52-week high, and December Fed hike odds to about 77–80%, a headwind for emerging-market currencies.

Goldman Sachs sees EGP 53 per dollar in three months and keeps its buy call, though it estimates foreign holdings of local debt fell to about $20bn from $30bn; the Cabinet also put foreign-currency spending under Finance Ministry approval.
The central bank's rate rose to EGP 54.31 from 54.01 after six straight falls, while the 91-day bill eased to 24.86% from 25.00%, a sign demand for local debt held.
Urban inflation slowed to 12.7% in October from 13.9%, leaving the 20% deposit rate 7.3 points above prices; the central bank's dollar rate fell to EGP 54.05.

The central bank's dollar rate fell to EGP 53.39, the pound's strongest in a year, after foreigners bought about $567m of local debt on Monday (exchange data via Al-Ain) and remittances hit a record $38.2bn for nine months (EnterpriseAM). Two independent dollar sources now back the call.

views.title: Brent stays below $105 while Iran talks continue
views.detail: Brent fell about 9% to roughly $95 on peace hopes; Goldman sees $105 by December, and Hormuz incidents keep a risk premium.

updates.text: Brent rose 3.9% to $98.29 after Iran exempted ships from four countries from Hormuz limits.
The US struck Iranian air defenses on Qeshm island and a third carrier heads for the region, raising the risk of renewed war; Brent held at $98.32.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers hit mines and caught fire in Hormuz, and the Houthis claimed strikes on Aramco sites; neither claim was confirmed and Brent had not yet traded on them.
Brent traded near $96 on Monday, down about 2%, after Trump called new strikes on Iran "highly unlikely" if talks progress; the Houthis' strike on Riyadh's Aramco tower caused only minor damage.
Brent fell 5.85% to $92.57 on Monday after President Trump said Iran was "effectively over" militarily following talks with Qatar's prime minister.
Brent settled 1.2% lower at $91.49 after briefly dipping below $90, then rose toward $92 after a tanker was attacked near Hormuz (CNBC, The National).

views.title: Egypt Aluminium returns to EGP 335–345 by end of December
views.detail: First-quarter profit rose 104% to EGP 4.93bn on sales up 6.4%, putting the stock at about 7.3 times the last 12 months' earnings at EGP 317.00, below its 50-day average of about EGP 338. A planned state stake sale is the risk to the timing.
